title: Neural Networks
tagline: Multilayer networks, backpropagation, optimisers, initialisation, normalisation and training practice
summary: Deep networks learn their own features. This course builds multilayer perceptrons, derives backpropagation and automatic differentiation, and covers the optimisers, initialisation, normalisation and regularisation that make deep networks trainable, with convolutional networks as a first architecture.

chapters.title: From perceptrons to multilayer networks
chapters.summary: Neurons, activation functions, multilayer perceptrons and universal approximation.

chapters.title: Backpropagation
chapters.summary: Computation graphs, the backward pass and the cost of computing gradients.

chapters.title: Automatic differentiation
chapters.summary: Forward and reverse mode, tensors and autograd systems such as PyTorch and JAX.

chapters.title: Optimisers
chapters.summary: SGD, momentum, RMSProp, Adam and AdamW, learning-rate schedules and warm-up.

chapters.title: Initialisation and normalisation
chapters.summary: Vanishing and exploding gradients, Xavier and He initialisation, batch and layer normalisation, and residual connections.

chapters.title: Regularisation in deep networks
chapters.summary: Dropout, weight decay, label smoothing, data augmentation and implicit regularisation.

chapters.title: Convolutional networks
chapters.summary: Convolutions, pooling, receptive fields and residual networks.

chapters.title: Training deep networks in practice
chapters.summary: Data pipelines, batching, mixed precision, debugging loss curves and reproducibility.
